correctness.rationale: The trace quadratic form Q(x)=Tr(ax^(p^h+1)+bx^2) has polar radical cut out by a x^(p^h)+a^(p^(2n-h))x^(p^(2n-h))+2bx=0 for n>=h; applying Frobenius yields an order-two semilinear recurrence over fixed field F_(p^d), d=gcd(h,2n), with invertible companion matrix. The fixed-vector lemma (minimal K-dependence of k-independent semilinear solutions) bounds radical dimension r<=2d over F_p, and each nonzero scalar quadratic Gauss sum has modulus p^(n+r/2). Triangle inequality gives the uniform bound; Hasse extremal deviation (p-1)p^(n+h) implies d=h. For n<h the Hasse value exceeds point-count constraints; n=h,b!=0 cannot have full polar radical because nontrivial Frobenius and identity maps are independent. Independent direct F9 trace and point count for nine (a,b) nonzero pairs corroborates boundary; the proof is symbolic for arbitrary p,n,h.
